evidence.quote: § 892.2060 Radiological computer-assisted diagnostic software for lesions suspicious of cancer.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: FDA regulation classifying radiological computer-assisted diagnostic software that characterizes lesions suspicious for cancer as Class II (special controls) image-processing devices. It sets design verification, validation and labeling requirements for manufacturers, with the clinical user making diagnostic decisions.
summary.long: The section identifies radiological computer-assisted diagnostic software for lesions suspicious of cancer as an image processing prescription device. It aids in characterizing lesions on images such as magnetic resonance, mammography, radiography or computed tomography, extracting features from the images and giving information about the lesions to the user. Diagnostic and patient management decisions remain with the clinical user. Paragraph (b) classifies the device as Class II (special controls). Design verification and validation must include a detailed description of the image analysis algorithms, pre-specified performance testing protocols, results showing the device improves reader performance in the intended use population, test datasets with sufficient cases from important cohorts, standalone performance testing, and software documentation including cybersecurity. Labeling must include the patient population, reading protocol, intended user and training, device inputs and outputs, compatible imaging hardware and protocols, warnings and limitations (including situations where the device may fail), instructions for use, and a detailed summary of performance testing with sub-analyses. The text states no numeric thresholds, enforcement measures or penalties.
